lines.text: In sixteen sixty-six, a tiny bakery fire burned down most of London.
It started just after midnight, in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane.
London was packed with wooden houses, and a strong wind was blowing,
so the flames jumped from roof to roof.
The Lord Mayor was woken up, but he shrugged it off.
For four days, the city burned.
Thirteen thousand houses, eighty-seven churches, and St Paul's Cathedral were gone.
In the end, they blew up whole streets to stop it spreading.
And when London was rebuilt, it was built in brick and stone.
All because of one small bakery.
